The Headmaster

Iskolaya · Kumana National Park, Sri Lanka

Hidden inside Kumana National Park are the remains of a village that was abandoned many years ago. The people are gone, and the jungle has grown in around what they left behind. But a few walls of the old village school are still standing.

A school with no children might sound like a lonely place. Not to one leopard. He made those old walls his favourite place to rest, and he became well known for lying stretched out along the top of them, fast asleep, as if he were the only student who never went home.

That is how he got his name: Iskolaya, from iskole, the Sinhala word for school.

On the day of this picture, Iskolaya had chosen a different bed, a tree not far from his schoolhouse. He was resting in the branches when he noticed us, and he stared straight back at us, studying us carefully, as if he were trying to figure out exactly what we were doing in his part of the forest.
